newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS - Australia lists Japan deregulation requests.
newsitem.headline: RTRS - Australia lists Japan deregulation requests.

text.p: Australian Trade Minister Tim Fischer said on Thursday that Australia had lodged a submission with the Japanese government outlining its priorities for deregulation in Japan.
Fischer said it was the government's third submission in relation to Japan's three-year Deregulation Action Programme.
The submission contains details of regulatory issues which either directly or indirectly affect Australian companies' access to Japanese markets.
Specific requests related to regulatory barriers covering land and housing issues, telecommunications, shipping issues, food and agricultural products, and other discriminatory trade practices.
Fischer said requests in these sectors were identified following close consultation with Australian industry.
"Australia will continue to take every opportunity to encourage Japan to continue to pursue further deregulation vigorously," he said in a statement.

"Australia hopes the Japanese government will allocate sufficient resources and give the support needed to implement the necessary structural changes which are in the interests of Japanese consumers and business as well as foreign suppliers."
On November 13, the Japanese government unveiled plans for deregulation in six major areas, including the financial sector and telecommunications, by 2001.

Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto has vowed to reduce the red tape that stifles entrepreneurs, keeps costs high, hampers imports and frustrates foreign companies trying to do business in Japan. -- Canberra Bureau 61-6 273-2730
